Multiaxis ECI · data of 2026-10-19 · K = 4 · 12 fits

Which MIRT model should we keep?

Six structures, each fitted on the AI models alone (humans placed afterwards, “2b”) and with the human tiers inside the fit. The goal: keep the one that finds real latent axes and dates, without a method artefact, when AI passes the domain expert, the committee of experts and the Top Performer.

The variants in brief

Six 4-axis MIRT structures
Flagship
Compensatory, free loadings, per-benchmark ceilings, lineage prior.
Free bifactor
A general factor g and 3 specifics, shown separately.
Bifactor g + deviations (gsum)
Each displayed axis is g plus its own deviation.
Orthogonal bifactor (orth)
g and the specifics constrained to be uncorrelated.
Simple structure (ss25)
A prior pushes each benchmark towards a single axis.
Pinned simple structure (pin)
ss25 with the axes' orientation fixed a priori.
Two ways to place the humans
Models only + 2b
Fit on the AI models (50 chains), then human tiers placed axis by axis, benchmarks frozen.
Humans in
The human tiers enter the fit (20 chains).

Verdict

  1. Keep the flagship (models only + 2b). Best LOO or tied, most reproducible mode (21 of 50 chains), four rising, nameable axes. Alternative: gsum, tied on LOO.
  2. Drop the humans-in fits. All six structures compensate (expert 4 to 7 SD below the frontier on one axis, 10 to 20 above on another) and predict the AI scores worse (−73 to −120 nats).
  3. Keep ss25 and pin as a check on the axes. Sharper axes, the same Science and Cyber axes, but −34 to −44 nats.
  4. All-axes dates are still fragile. Expert: ≈ 2037 (flagship), ≈ mid-2030 (gsum). Committee of experts and Top Performer: only bounds, for lack of scores. The bottleneck is the commonsense axis.

Scorecard

“AI prediction”: integrated LOO of the AI scores against the flagship (mode A), on the reliable observations.

Selected mode: chains in the mode / total · number of modes. Sharpness: mean share of each benchmark's dominant axis (1 = one axis per benchmark).

Pros and cons of the variants kept

What is still fragile for goal 2

  • Too few scores for the committee of experts (3 benchmarks) and the Top Performer (4). They are placed on only 1 to 3 axes. These are the data to acquire first, in agentic, cyber and commonsense.
  • The commonsense axis is the bottleneck. Slowest slope, saturated benchmarks, expert without a score of its own; widening it to scientific knowledge makes the placement incoherent (tested on 2026-11-06).
  • The 2b placement is still an assumption (other axes at the typical-model profile, content judgments), but it is the only method tested without compensation, including against placing the tiers on all 4 axes at once.
